### testFlow3dEoc

This app implements a Navier--Stokes flow with an analytical solution [@krause:10b].
The *standard* simulation as well as an EOC computation for various error norms are shown.
The implementation makes use of the Solver framework, while simulation parameters are read from the corresponding parameter XML file.
Among others, the following options can be selected:

- The flow domain can be either a cube or restricted to a sphere (node `[Application][Domain]`).
- Different LBM boundary conditions, all of them implementing a Dirichlet fixed velocity (node `[Application][BoundaryCondition]`).

Especially, the EOC computation can be used to benchmark various aspects of LBM implementation, e.g. the boundary conditions and the collision steps.
The results of an example run are shown in @fig-tf-eoc.

![EOC study for the example on a sphere, as it is returned via the `gnuplot` interface.](/examples/pdeSolverEoc/testFlow3dEoc/doc/fig/tf_eoc.png){#fig-tf-eoc width="80%"}

The class structure is as follows: `TestFlowBase` implements the basic simulation details (geometry, boundary conditions etc.).
Since it shall later be used for adjoint optimization, it inherits from `AdjointLbSolverBase`.
The specification `TestFlowSolver` then implements the standard simulation.
The distinction between `TestFlowBase` and `TestFlowSolver` is solely because `TestFlowBase` will also be used for optimization.
